title: The Little Book of Lykke: The Danish Search for the World's Happiest People
author: Meik Wiking
target_audience: Readers interested in happiness and well-being
People curious about Danish and Scandinavian culture
Readers who enjoyed 'The Little Book of Hygge'
Anyone seeking practical tips to increase happiness in everyday life
core_themes: Global perspectives on happiness and well-being
Practical ways individuals and societies can foster happiness
primary_purpose: To explore what makes people happy throughout the world, highlighting Danish and global research on happiness, and to inspire readers with evidence-based tips and heartwarming stories for living a happier, more fulfilling life.

structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic chapters focusing on different happiness factors (togetherness, money, health, freedom, trust, kindness)
features: Real-life stories and interviews from around the world

key_concepts_lessons: Happiness is multifaceted and found across many cultures, not just in Denmark.
Small actions—like sharing meals or helping neighbors—significantly boost happiness.
Social connections and a sense of community are key to well-being.
Trust, both interpersonally and in institutions, is linked to higher happiness.
Living with purpose, freedom, and balance enhances life satisfaction.
Civic engagement, generosity, and random acts of kindness benefit both giver and receiver.
Happiness can be ‘built’ through daily habits and mindful choices.
notable_features: Based on research by the Happiness Research Institute in Copenhagen
Blends scientific studies with practical advice and touching stories
Illustrated with photographs, infographics, and “lykke” tips
Global perspective with examples from many countries
Complementary follow-up to 'The Little Book of Hygge'
cultural_historical_context: Published amid global fascination with Scandinavian well-being, ‘lykke’ (pronounced loo-ka; Danish for ‘happiness’) explores universal elements of happiness at a time when mental health and community were prominent international concerns.
reception_impact: Became an international bestseller, translated into multiple languages
Praised for its warmth and uplifting message
Appreciated for its practical advice and global, inclusive perspective
Considered a go-to happiness guide and coffee-table book
Some critics found advice light or anecdotal compared to in-depth scientific texts
comparable_titles: The Little Book of Hygge by Meik Wiking
The Art of Making Memories by Meik Wiking
The Happiness Project by Gretchen Rubin
The Blue Zones of Happiness by Dan Buettner
The Book of Joy by Dalai Lama and Desmond Tutu
